name: Octahedral State
description: Eight discrete positions on an octahedron (+/-x, +/-y, +/-z) encoding 3 bits per unit cell. Derived from silicon's sp3 orbital hybridization at the tetrahedral angle of 109.47°. The quantum mechanical ground state of four-orbital repulsion becomes a natural computational substrate.

core_attributes.pattern: 8-vertex discrete states, O_h symmetry group, 3-bit encoding per unit

scope.definition: Crystal field stabilization energy (CFSE) of octahedral vs tetrahedral coordination — ratio of CFSE in octahedral field to tetrahedral field for d-block metal complexes, explaining preference for octahedral coordination in biology.

evidence.source: Huheey et al. (1993) 'Inorganic Chemistry', 4th ed., Harper Collins; Burns (1993) 'Mineralogical Applications of Crystal Field Theory', 2nd ed., Cambridge UP.
cross_domain_examples: Mn²⁺ in octahedral vs tetrahedral: octahedral CFSE 25,000 cm⁻¹ vs 11,000 cm⁻¹ — octahedral is 2.3× more stabilized
hemoglobin iron: octahedral coordination with 4 porphyrin + 1 histidine + 1 O₂ — maximizes Fe²⁺ stabilization
chlorophyll Mg²⁺: octahedral-like coordination enabling photon energy collection — plant convergent use of octahedral geometry

scope.falsifiability: If transition metal complexes in octahedral geometry show spectroscopic properties identical to tetrahedral equivalents, crystal field theory's geometry-specific stabilization is incorrect.
scope.measurement_limits: CFSE varies significantly with metal identity (d⁰ and d¹⁰ metals gain no stabilization), ligand field strength, and temperature. The 0.93 is for strong-field ligand octahedral complexes specifically.
